newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's CAP studies new copper mines.
newsitem.headline: Chile's CAP studies new copper mines.

text.p: Chilean steel-maker Compania de Aceros del Pacifico (CAP) is studying the development of several small copper deposits in central and northern Chile, said finance manager Jaime Charles.
"We are looking at five or six projects on a small scale in the Third and Fourth Region," Charles told reporters at a mining seminar in Santiago.
"The study is still very preliminary and it could take another two years to carry out feasibility studies."
Charles said the deposits would each produce between 20,000 and 30,000 tonnes of fine copper a year.
CAP, Chile's largest steel producer, already owns a 27 percent stake in the Carmen de Andacollo copper mine which was officially opened in April.
The mine's owners, which include Canada Tungsten Inc, have plans to expand the 20,000-tonne a year mine in the long term, said Charles.
"There are plans to expand the mine in 10 years' time which could increase its output five or six times to 100,000 or 150,000 tonnes," he said.
Andacollo currently exploits oxide reserves but the expansion would mine a large sulphide deposit lying beneath the oxides, he said.
The pit is 63 percent owned by Canada Tungsten with the rest held by Chile's state mining company Enami.
